Medhatiths (p. 144, 1. 138)— Arthavadoyam parakrti-
nama’—There are several classifications of Arthavada passages.
The one referred to here is that into the four kinds~—(1)
‘Stuti’ (2) ‘Ninda’, (3) ‘Parakrti’ and ‘ Purakalpa’—mentioned
in the Nyayasiitra of Gautama (2. 1. 65), under which Vatsya-
yana gives examples of each kind:—(1) ‘Stute’, Valedictory—
is the name given to that text which eulogises a certain
injunction by describing the desirable results following from
the enjoined act ;—(2) the text that describes the undesirable
results following from the act is called ‘nenda’, ‘Depreca-
tory ’;—(3) the text that describes a contrary method of action
adopted by a certain person is called ‘ parakrtz’, ‘illustrative’;
—and (4) that which describes a method as adopted tradi-
tionally is called Purdkalpa, ‘ Narrative’.
Another classification of the Arthavada is into three
kinds—(1) Descriptive by indirect implication, (2) Descriptive
by direct intimation and (3) Descriptive of an accomplished
fact.
The Mimamsa-bala-prakasha (pp. 48-58) describes no
less than 38 kinds of Arthavada (see Prabhakara Mimamsa,
pp. 115-116)

in both cases|—The conclusion therefore is that the name
‘Upanayana’ pertains to the imparting ‘of the Gayatri-
mantra.
